sanskrit: vyūhayantrāyudhīyānāṃ tattvajño vikramānvitaḥ varṣaśītoṣṇavātānāṃ sahiṣṇuḥ pararandhravit
english: Let him be one who truly knows battle-arrays, engines, and weapons, endowed with valor, enduring of rain and cold and heat and wind, and skilled at detecting the weak points of his foes.

sanskrit: viśvāsayet parāṃś caiva viśvasen na tu kasya cit putreṣv api hi rājendra viśvāso na praśasyate
english: Let him inspire confidence in others, yet himself trust no one; for even in one's sons, O lord of kings, trust is not to be commended.

sanskrit: etac chāstrārthatattvaṃ tu tavākhyātaṃ mayānagha aviśvāso narendrāṇāṃ guhyaṃ paramam ucyate
english: This essence of the meaning of the treatises I have declared to you, O sinless one; mistrust is said to be the supreme secret of kings.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃvidhaṃ puraṃ rājā svayam āvastum arhati kṛtaṃ vā kārayitvā vā tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In what kind of city ought a king himself to dwell — one already built, or one he has caused to be built? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yatra kaunteya vastavyaṃ saputrabhrātṛbandhunā nyāyyaṃ tatra paripraṣṭuṃ guptiṃ vṛttiṃ ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: Where one must dwell, O son of Kuntī, together with sons and brothers and kinsmen, it is right there to inquire into its defenses and its means of livelihood, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasmāt te vartayiṣyāmi durgakarma viśeṣataḥ śrutvā tathā vidhātavyam anuṣṭheyaṃ ca yatnataḥ
english: Therefore I shall set forth for you the matter of fortifications in particular; having heard it, you should so dispose things and carry them out with care.

sanskrit: ṣaḍvidhaṃ durgam āsthāya purāṇy atha niveśayet sarvasaṃpatpradhānaṃ yad bāhulyaṃ vāpi saṃbhavet
english: Resorting to fortification of six kinds, let him establish cities — whichever abounds chiefly in all resources, or wherever such abundance may be possible.

sanskrit: dhanvadurgaṃ mahīdurgaṃ giridurgaṃ tathaiva ca manuṣyadurgam abdurgaṃ vanadurgaṃ ca tāni ṣaṭ
english: A desert-fort, an earthwork-fort, a hill-fort, likewise a fort of men, a water-fort, and a forest-fort — these are the six.

sanskrit: yat puraṃ durgasaṃpannaṃ dhānyāyudhasamanvitam dṛḍhaprākāraparikhaṃ hastyaśvarathasaṃkulam
english: That city which is well provided with defenses, furnished with grain and weapons, with stout ramparts and moats, and thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots —

sanskrit: vidvāṃsaḥ śilpino yatra nicayāś ca susaṃcitāḥ dhārmikaś ca jano yatra dākṣyam uttamam āsthitaḥ
english: where there are learned men and craftsmen, and stores well laid up, and where the people are righteous and have attained the highest skill;

sanskrit: ūrjasvinaranāgāśvaṃ catvarāpaṇaśobhitam prasiddhavyavahāraṃ ca praśāntam akutobhayam
english: vigorous in its men, elephants, and horses, graced with crossroads and markets, of well-established commerce, tranquil, and with nothing to fear from any quarter;

sanskrit: suprabhaṃ sānunādaṃ ca supraśastaniveśanam śūrāḍhyajanasaṃpannaṃ brahmaghoṣānunāditam
english: radiant, resounding, with well-ordered dwellings, filled with people who are brave and wealthy, and made to echo with the chanting of the Veda —

sanskrit: samājotsavasaṃpannaṃ sadāpūjitadaivatam vaśyāmātyabalo rājā tat puraṃ svayam āvaset
english: abounding in assemblies and festivals, where the gods are ever worshipped: in such a city let the king, with ministers and army obedient to him, himself dwell.

sanskrit: tatra kośaṃ balaṃ mitraṃ vyavahāraṃ ca vardhayet pure janapade caiva sarvadoṣān nivartayet
english: There let him increase his treasury, his army, his allies, and his commerce, and let him do away with every defect in city and countryside alike.

sanskrit: bhāṇḍāgārāyudhāgāraṃ prayatnenābhivardhayet nicayān vardhayet sarvāṃs tathā yantragadāgadān
english: With diligence let him enlarge his storehouses and armories, and increase all his stores, his engines of war, his maces, and his medicines.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhalohatuṣāṅgāradāruśṛṅgāsthivaiṇavān majjāsnehavasākṣaudram auṣadhagrāmam eva ca
english: Timber, iron, chaff, charcoal, planks, horn, bone, and bamboo; marrow, oil, fat, and honey, and a whole supply of medicinal herbs —

sanskrit: śaṇaṃ sarjarasaṃ dhānyam āyudhāni śarāṃs tathā carma snāyu tathā vetraṃ muñjabalbajadhanvanān
english: hemp, resin, grain, weapons and arrows, hides and sinews, and cane, and muñja and balbaja grasses and the wood of the dhanvana tree.

sanskrit: āśayāś codapānāś ca prabhūtasalilā varāḥ niroddhavyāḥ sadā rājñā kṣīriṇaś ca mahīruhāḥ
english: Reservoirs and wells, excellent and abounding in water, should ever be kept secure by the king, and so too the trees that yield sap.

sanskrit: satkṛtāś ca prayatnena ācāryartvikpurohitāḥ maheṣvāsāḥ sthapatayaḥ sāṃvatsaracikitsakāḥ
english: And with care let him honor teachers, officiating priests, and chaplains; mighty archers, architects, astrologers, and physicians;

sanskrit: prājñā medhāvino dāntā dakṣāḥ śūrā bahuśrutāḥ kulīnāḥ sattvasaṃpannā yuktāḥ sarveṣu karmasu
english: the wise, the intelligent, the self-controlled, the able, the brave, the deeply learned, the well-born, the men of great spirit, fit for every task.

sanskrit: pūjayed dhārmikān rājā nigṛhṇīyād adhārmikān niyuñjyāc ca prayatnena sarvavarṇān svakarmasu
english: Let the king honor the righteous and restrain the unrighteous, and with diligence set all the classes to their proper tasks.

sanskrit: bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ caiva paurajānapadaṃ janam cāraiḥ suviditaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ karma prayojayet
english: Having made well known through his spies the people of city and country, both without and within, let him then set his measures in motion.

sanskrit: cārān mantraṃ ca kośaṃ ca mantraṃ caiva viśeṣataḥ anutiṣṭhet svayaṃ rājā sarvaṃ hy atra pratiṣṭhitam
english: To his spies, his counsel, and his treasury — and to his counsel above all — let the king himself attend; for upon these everything rests.

sanskrit: udāsīnārimitrāṇāṃ sarvam eva cikīrṣitam pure janapade caiva jñātavyaṃ cāracakṣuṣā
english: Whatever the neutral, the foe, and the ally intend to do, in city and country alike, is to be known through the eye of his spies.

sanskrit: tatas tathā vidhātavyaṃ sarvam evāpramādataḥ bhaktān pujayatā nityaṃ dviṣataś ca nigṛhṇatā
english: Thereupon let everything be so ordered without negligence, the king ever honoring the loyal and restraining the hostile.

sanskrit: yaṣṭavyaṃ kratubhir nityaṃ dātavyaṃ cāpy apīḍayā prajānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ na kāryaṃ karma garhitam
english: He should ever sacrifice with sacrifices, and give gifts without oppression; the protection of the people is to be done, and no blameworthy deed is to be done.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇānāthavṛddhānāṃ vidhavānāṃ ca yoṣitām yogakṣemaṃ ca vṛttiṃ ca nityam eva prakalpayet
english: For the wretched, the helpless, and the aged, and for widowed women, let him ever provide both welfare and livelihood.

sanskrit: āśrameṣu yathākālaṃ celabhājanabhojanam sadaivopahared rājā satkṛtyānavamanya ca
english: To the hermitages, at the proper seasons, let the king ever bring clothing, vessels, and food, doing them honor and never holding them in contempt.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ sarvakāryāṇi tāpase rājyam eva ca nivedayet prayatnena tiṣṭhet prahvaś ca sarvadā
english: Himself, all his affairs, and even his kingdom let him diligently lay before the ascetic, and ever stand before him in humility.

sanskrit: sarvārthatyāginaṃ rājā kule jātaṃ bahuśrutam pūjayet tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā śayanāsanabhojanaiḥ
english: One who has renounced all possessions, born of good family and deeply learned — seeing such a one, let the king honor him with bed, seat, and food.

sanskrit: tasmin kurvīta viśvāsaṃ rājā kasyāṃ cid āpadi tāpaseṣu hi viśvāsam api kurvanti dasyavaḥ
english: In him let the king place his trust in any time of distress; for even robbers place their trust in ascetics.

sanskrit: tasmin nidhīn ādadhīta prajñāṃ paryādadīta ca na cāpy abhīkṣṇaṃ seveta bhṛśaṃ vā pratipūjayet
english: With him let him deposit his treasures and from him gather wisdom; yet let him not wait upon him too constantly, nor honor him to excess.

sanskrit: anyaḥ kāryaḥ svarāṣṭreṣu pararāṣṭreṣu cāparaḥ aṭavīṣv aparaḥ kāryaḥ sāmantanagareṣu ca
english: One such man should be employed within his own realm, another in foreign realms, another in the forests, and another in the cities of bordering princes.

sanskrit: teṣu satkārasaṃskārān saṃvibhāgāṃś ca kārayet pararāṣṭrāṭavīstheṣu yathā svaviṣaye tathā
english: To those stationed in foreign realms and forests let him render the same honors, attentions, and shares as to those within his own domain.

sanskrit: te kasyāṃ cid avasthāyāṃ śaraṇaṃ śaraṇārthine rājñe dadyur yathākāmaṃ tāpasāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: In any such circumstance, those ascetics of rigorous vows will, at his wish, grant refuge to the king who seeks refuge.

sanskrit: eṣa te lakṣaṇoddeśaḥ saṃkṣepeṇa prakīrtitaḥ yādṛśaṃ nagaraṃ rājā svayam āvastum arhati
english: This, in brief, is the summary of the marks I have declared to you — of the kind of city in which a king ought himself to dwell.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rāṣṭraguptiṃ ca me rājan rāṣṭrasyaiva ca saṃgraham samyag jijñāsamānāya prabrūhi bharatarṣabha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: To me who would rightly understand it, O king, declare the protection of the realm and likewise the gathering-in of the realm, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rāṣṭraguptiṃ ca te samyag rāṣṭrasyaiva ca saṃgraham hanta sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi tattvam ekamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: Bhīṣma said: The protection of the realm and the gathering-in of the realm — come, I shall declare it all to you rightly; listen with single-minded attention to the truth.

sanskrit: grāmasyādhipatiḥ kāryo daśagrāmyas tathāparaḥ dviguṇāyāḥ śatasyaivaṃ sahasrasya ca kārayet
english: A headman should be appointed for a village, another over ten villages, another over twice that number, and so over a hundred, and over a thousand let him likewise appoint one.

sanskrit: grāme yān grāmadoṣāṃś ca grāmikaḥ paripālayet tān brūyād daśapāyāsau sa tu viṃśatipāya vai
english: Whatever faults of the village the village-headman has to keep watch over, let him report to the lord of ten; and he in turn to the lord of twenty.

sanskrit: so 'pi viṃśatyadhipatir vṛttaṃ jānapade jane grāmāṇāṃ śatapālāya sarvam eva nivedayet
english: And that lord of twenty should report all the doings among the country-folk to the protector of a hundred villages.

sanskrit: yāni grāmīṇabhojyāni grāmikas tāny upāśnuyāt daśapas tena bhartavyas tenāpi dviguṇādhipaḥ
english: Whatever the village affords for enjoyment, the village-headman may partake of; by him the lord of ten is to be maintained, and by the latter the lord of twenty.

sanskrit: grāmaṃ grāmaśatādhyakṣo bhoktum arhati satkṛtaḥ mahāntaṃ bharataśreṣṭha susphītajanasaṃkulam tatra hy anekam āyattaṃ rājño bhavati bhārata
english: The overseer of a hundred villages, held in honor, is entitled to enjoy a village — a great one, O best of the Bharatas, thronged with prosperous people; for therein much that belongs to the king is at stake, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śākhānagaram arhas tu sahasrapatir uttamam dhānyahairaṇyabhogena bhoktuṃ rāṣṭriya udyataḥ
english: But the lord of a thousand deserves a great market-town as his portion; that high officer of the realm is entitled to enjoy it through the revenue of grain and gold.

sanskrit: tathā yad grāmakṛtyaṃ syād grāmikṛtyaṃ ca te svayam dharmajñaḥ sacivaḥ kaś cit tat prapaśyed atandritaḥ
english: And whatever pertains to the village's business and the headman's duty, some minister versed in dharma should himself oversee, unwearied.

sanskrit: nagare nagare ca syād ekaḥ sarvārthacintakaḥ uccaiḥsthāne ghorarūpo nakṣatrāṇām iva grahaḥ bhavet sa tān parikrāmet sarvān eva sadā svayam
english: In every city there should be one superintendent of all affairs, set on high and of awesome aspect, like a planet among the stars; let him ever make his rounds over them all himself.

sanskrit: vikrayaṃ krayam adhvānaṃ bhaktaṃ ca saparivyayam yogakṣemaṃ ca saṃprekṣya vaṇijaḥ kārayet karān
english: Considering the selling, the buying, the road-tolls, the provisioning together with its costs, and the safe conduct of goods, let him levy the taxes upon the merchants.

sanskrit: utpattiṃ dānavṛttiṃ ca śilpaṃ saṃprekṣya cāsakṛt śilpapratikarān eva śilpinaḥ prati kārayet
english: Considering again and again the output, the cost of materials, and the craft itself, let him impose upon the artisans dues proportioned to their craft.

sanskrit: uccāvacakarā nyāyyāḥ pūrvarājñāṃ yudhiṣṭhira yathā yathā na hīyeraṃs tathā kuryān mahīpatiḥ
english: The taxes, high and low, were justly fixed by the kings of old, Yudhiṣṭhira; the lord of earth should so act that they suffer no diminution.

sanskrit: phalaṃ karma ca saṃprekṣya tataḥ sarvaṃ prakalpayet phalaṃ karma ca nirhetu na kaś cit saṃpravartayet
english: Considering both the yield and the labor, let him then apportion everything; for no one undertakes either yield or labor without a motive.

sanskrit: yathā rājā ca kartā ca syātāṃ karmaṇi bhāginau samavekṣya tathā rājñā praṇeyāḥ satataṃ karāḥ
english: So that both the king and the laborer may be sharers in the work — considering this, the taxes should ever be levied by the king.

sanskrit: nocchindyād ātmano mūlaṃ pareṣāṃ vāpi tṛṣṇayā īhādvārāṇi saṃrudhya rājā saṃprītidarśanaḥ
english: Out of greed let him not cut off his own root, nor that of others, by blocking the avenues of their enterprise; rather let the king be of gracious aspect.

sanskrit: pradviṣanti parikhyātaṃ rājānam atikhādinam pradviṣṭasya kutaḥ śreyaḥ saṃpriyo labhate priyam
english: Men come to hate a king notorious as a devourer of too much; whence comes good to one who is hated? The well-loved obtains what is dear to him.

sanskrit: vatsaupamyena dogdhavyaṃ rāṣṭram akṣīṇabuddhinā bhṛto vatso jātabalaḥ pīḍāṃ sahati bhārata
english: The realm should be milked, as it were a calf, by a king of undiminished judgment; for the calf, once nourished and grown strong, can bear the strain, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na karma kurute vatso bhṛśaṃ dugdho yudhiṣṭhira rāṣṭram apy atidugdhaṃ hi na karma kurute mahat
english: A calf milked too hard does no work, Yudhiṣṭhira; and a realm too heavily milked likewise performs no great labor.

sanskrit: yo rāṣṭram anugṛhṇāti parigṛhya svayaṃ nṛpaḥ saṃjātam upajīvan sa labhate sumahat phalam
english: That king who, having taken the realm in hand, cherishes it, and lives upon what it brings forth, obtains a very great fruit.

sanskrit: āpadarthaṃ hi nicayān rājāna iha cinvate rāṣṭraṃ ca kośabhūtaṃ syāt kośo veśmagatas tathā
english: For against a time of distress do kings here heap up their stores; the realm itself should be as a treasury, and the treasury kept within the palace.

sanskrit: paurajānapadān sarvān saṃśritopāśritāṃs tathā yathāśakty anukampeta sarvān abhyantarān api
english: Upon all the townsfolk and country-folk, and those who have sought his shelter or come near it, and upon all his intimates as well, let him have compassion as far as he is able.

sanskrit: bāhyaṃ janaṃ bhedayitvā bhoktavyo madhyamaḥ sukham evaṃ na saṃprakupyante janāḥ sukhitaduḥkhitāḥ
english: Having divided off the outer folk, the middling sort may be drawn upon at ease; thus the people, whether well-off or hard-pressed, do not grow wrathful.

sanskrit: prāg eva tu karādānam anubhāṣya punaḥ punaḥ saṃnipatya svaviṣaye bhayaṃ rāṣṭre pradarśayet
english: But before levying the tax, having spoken of it again and again, let him assemble the people in his domain and set before the realm the danger that threatens it:

sanskrit: iyam āpat samutpannā paracakrabhayaṃ mahat api nāntāya kalpeta veṇor iva phalāgamaḥ
english: "This calamity has arisen, a great peril of an invading host; it may well end in destruction, as the bamboo's bearing of fruit ends in its death."

sanskrit: arayo me samutthāya bahubhir dasyubhiḥ saha idam ātmavadhāyaiva rāṣṭram icchanti bādhitum
english: "My foes have risen up together with many bandits, and seek to crush this realm to its very ruin."

sanskrit: asyām āpadi ghorāyāṃ saṃprāpte dāruṇe bhaye paritrāṇāya bhavatāṃ prārthayiṣye dhanāni vaḥ
english: "In this dread calamity now come upon us, in this terrible peril, for your own deliverance I shall ask of you your wealth."

sanskrit: pratidāsye ca bhavatāṃ sarvaṃ cāhaṃ bhayakṣaye nārayaḥ pratidāsyanti yad dhareyur balād itaḥ
english: "And when the danger is past I shall repay it all to you; but the foes, should they carry it off by force from here, will make no repayment."

sanskrit: kalatram āditaḥ kṛtvā naśyet svaṃ svayam eva hi api cet putradārārtham arthasaṃcaya iṣyate
english: "Putting one's wife and family first of all, a man's wealth perishes of itself — even though wealth be hoarded for the very sake of children and wife."

sanskrit: nandāmi vaḥ prabhāvena putrāṇām iva codaye yathāśakty anugṛhṇāmi rāṣṭrasyāpīḍayā ca vaḥ
english: "I rejoice in your prosperity as in the rising fortune of my own sons; and as far as I am able, I favor you, without oppressing the realm."

sanskrit: āpatsv eva ca voḍhavyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ sadgavair iva na vaḥ priyataraṃ kāryaṃ dhanaṃ kasyāṃ cid āpadi
english: "In times of distress alone is the burden to be borne by you, like good oxen; in no calamity is there anything you hold dearer than wealth."

sanskrit: iti vācā madhurayā ślakṣṇayā sopacārayā svaraśmīn abhyavasṛjed yugam ādāya kālavit
english: With words sweet, gentle, and courteous like these, let the king, knowing the proper season, take up the yoke and slacken his own reins.

sanskrit: pracāraṃ bhṛtyabharaṇaṃ vyayaṃ gogrāmato bhayam yogakṣemaṃ ca saṃprekṣya gominaḥ kārayet karān
english: Considering the pasturage, the keeping of servants, the expense, the danger to herds and villages, and their welfare and safety, let him levy the taxes upon the herdsmen.

sanskrit: upekṣitā hi naśyeyur gomino 'raṇyavāsinaḥ tasmāt teṣu viśeṣeṇa mṛdupūrvaṃ samācaret
english: For if neglected, the herdsmen who dwell in the wilds would be ruined; therefore toward them in particular let him act with gentleness foremost.

sanskrit: sāntvanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānam avasthā cāpy abhīkṣṇaśaḥ gomināṃ pārtha kartavyaṃ saṃvibhāgāḥ priyāṇi ca
english: Conciliation, protection, gifts, and steady care — these are ever to be shown to the herdsmen, O Pārtha, with fair shares and kindnesses.

sanskrit: ajasram upayoktavyaṃ phalaṃ gomiṣu sarvataḥ prabhāvayati rāṣṭraṃ ca vyavahāraṃ kṛṣiṃ tathā
english: The fruit to be drawn from the herdsmen is to be used unceasingly on every side; it enriches the realm, and commerce, and tillage too.

sanskrit: tasmād gomiṣu yatnena prītiṃ kuryād vicakṣaṇaḥ dayāvān apramattaś ca karān saṃpraṇayan mṛdūn
english: Therefore the discerning king should with diligence foster the goodwill of the herdsmen, being compassionate and vigilant, and levying upon them only gentle taxes.

sanskrit: sarvatra kṣemacaraṇaṃ sulabhaṃ tāta gomibhiḥ na hy ataḥ sadṛśaṃ kiṃ cid dhanam asti yudhiṣṭhira
english: Everywhere, my son, security of movement is easily had through the herdsmen; for there is no wealth, Yudhiṣṭhira, to compare with this.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yadā rājā samartho 'pi kośārthī syān mahāmate kathaṃ pravarteta tadā tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a king, though capable, finds himself in need of treasure, O great-minded one, how should he then proceed? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yathādeśaṃ yathākālam api caiva yathābalam anuśiṣyāt prajā rājā dharmārthī taddhite rataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: According to place, according to time, and according to their capacity, let the king, seeking dharma and devoted to their welfare, direct his subjects.

sanskrit: yathā tāsāṃ ca manyeta śreya ātmana eva ca tathā dharmyāṇi sarvāṇi rājā rāṣṭre pravartayet
english: In such wise as he judges to be for their good and for his own, let the king set in motion all righteous works throughout the realm.

sanskrit: madhudohaṃ duhed rāṣṭraṃ bhramarān na vipātayet vatsāpekṣī duhec caiva stanāṃś ca na vikuṭṭayet
english: Let him milk the realm as one gathers honey, without destroying the bees; let him milk it with regard for the calf, and not lacerate the teats.

sanskrit: jalaukāvat pibed rāṣṭraṃ mṛdunaiva narādhipa vyāghrīva ca haret putram adaṣṭvā mā pated iti
english: Let him drink from the realm gently, as a leech does, O lord of men; and let him carry it as a tigress carries her cub — without biting, lest it fall.

sanskrit: alpenālpena deyena vardhamānaṃ pradāpayet tato bhūyas tato bhūyaḥ kāmaṃ vṛddhiṃ samācaret
english: By little and little of what is owed, let him cause the increasing yield to be paid; then more and more, at will, let him bring about its growth.
